dificultadDesc: Moderate. Varied terrain with some mountain stages and good infrastructure.
descripcion: The classic route par excellence. Starting from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, it crosses the most iconic landscapes of Navarra, La Rioja, Castilla and Galicia.
descripcionLarga: The French Way is the Jacobean route with the greatest historical tradition and the most internationally recognized.
It crosses the north of the Iberian Peninsula from Roncesvalles to Santiago de Compostela.
It is a transformative experience full of culture, art, and nature.
puntosDestacados: Crossing the Pyrenees from France
The Cathedral of Burgos and León
The Iron Cross in Astorga
The mystical arrival in O Cebreiro
Triumphant entry into the Plaza del Obradoiro

etapas.desc: Hard stage crossing the Pyrenees.
Descent through lush Navarrese forests.

dificultadDesc: Easy. Predominantly flat and gentle terrain, with some moderate difficulty stages.
descripcion: The Galician section of the Portuguese Way, starting in Tui next to the Minho river. The most popular option to complete the required kilometers for the Compostela in a week.
descripcionLarga: The Portuguese Way from Tui is the Galician section of the most frequented international Jacobean route. Tui, a historic city next to the Minho river, is one of the most popular starting points because from here you complete the kilometers needed to obtain the Compostela.

The route combines rural paths, small Galician villages, forests, and landscapes of the Rías Baixas. Throughout the stages, you pass through municipalities like O Porriño, Redondela, Pontevedra, Caldas de Reis, and Padrón before arriving in Santiago de Compostela.

It is an accessible, well-signposted route with excellent infrastructure for the pilgrim, ideal both for those making their debut on the Camino and for those who want to enjoy a quiet week walking through Galicia.
puntosDestacados: The Cathedral of Santa María de Tui and its medieval historic center
The Town Hall of O Porriño, work of Antonio Palacios
The railway viaducts of Redondela
The historic center of Pontevedra and the Basilica of Santa María la Mayor
The Segade Waterfall on the stage to Caldas de Reis
Padrón and its Jacobean tradition: the Church of Santiago de Padrón
Arrival at the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela

etapas.desc: Tui is one of the most popular starting points for the Portuguese Way to Santiago, as the necessary kilometers to obtain the Compostela are completed from here. This historic city located next to the Minho river preserves a beautiful old town and a great pilgrim atmosphere.
puntosInteres: Cathedral of Santa María de Tui, located at the top of the city
Medieval historic center with its cobblestone streets
Chapel of San Telmo, dedicated to the city's patron saint
River walk along the Minho river and views towards Valença (Portugal)

etapas.desc: First stage of the Portuguese Way in Galicia. The route alternates rural paths, small population centers, and quiet areas among forests and fields.
puntosInteres: Small rural churches and traditional cruceiros of the Portuguese Way
Town Hall of O Porriño, work of the architect Antonio Palacios

etapas.desc: The stage crosses the municipality of Mos and combines forest stretches with small villages and traditional paths of the Portuguese Way.
puntosInteres: Chapel of Santiaguiño de Antas, a place with great Jacobean tradition
Railway viaducts of Redondela, dominating the municipality's landscape

etapas.desc: One of the most pleasant stages of the Portuguese Way, with paths among forests and traditional roads crossing rural areas.
puntosInteres: Views towards the Vigo estuary during some sections of the route
Basilica of Santa María la Mayor in Pontevedra
Plaza de la Leña and Sanctuary of the Pilgrim Virgin in Pontevedra

etapas.desc: Quiet stage crossing rural landscapes, vineyards, and small typical Galician villages.
puntosInteres: Historic bridges of the Camino and natural areas next to the river
Segade Waterfall, one of the best-known natural corners of the area
Thermal tradition of Caldas de Reis

etapas.desc: The Camino continues through forests, villages, and rural paths until reaching one of the places with the greatest Jacobean tradition.
puntosInteres: Town of Padrón, closely linked to the history of the Apostle Santiago
Church of Santiago de Padrón, where according to tradition the pedrón related to the arrival of the Apostle's remains is preserved

etapas.desc: Last stage before reaching Santiago de Compostela. The route crosses small towns and rural areas until approaching the Galician capital.
puntosInteres: Historic center of Santiago de Compostela, declared a World Heritage Site
Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela, goal of the Camino and one of the most important pilgrimage sites in the world

dificultadDesc: Moderate. Mainly flat coastal terrain with sandy paths and medium-to-long distance stages.
descripcion: Complete Atlantic route from monumental Porto to Santiago de Compostela. Walk across wooden boardwalks over ocean beaches, fishing villages, the Minho river ferry crossing, and the Galician coast.
descripcionLarga: The Coastal Portuguese Way from Porto is one of the most stunning coastal experiences among all Jacobean paths. It starts in the historic Douro city and heads north following beaches and wooden walkways along the Portuguese Atlantic shore.

Throughout the stages, pilgrims pass through coastal towns rich in seafaring tradition such as Vila do Conde, Esposende, Viana do Castelo, and Caminha, where the iconic ferry crossing takes you across the Minho River into Galicia (A Guarda).

In Galicia, the trail follows the ocean through Oia and Baiona, climbs along trails overlooking the Vigo estuary, and merges in Redondela with the central way towards the Obradoiro Square in Santiago.
puntosDestacados: Departure from Porto following the Douro River to the Atlantic
Wooden boardwalks, sand dunes, and lighthouses of the Portuguese coast
Mount Santa Luzia in Viana do Castelo with panoramic ocean vistas
Scenic ferry crossing of the Minho River to A Guarda
Monastery of Santa María de Oia facing the ocean waves
Monterreal Fortress and historic harbour in Baiona
Stunning views of the Vigo estuary and viaducts of Redondela
Grand arrival at the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela

etapas.desc: Departure from Porto following the Douro River to the Atlantic. First contact with the sea, beaches, and wooden boardwalks.
Very coastal stage with dunes, lighthouses, and fishing villages. Very flat and pleasant.
One of the most beautiful sections. Arrival in Viana do Castelo with the option to climb Mount Santa Luzia (spectacular views).
Long but gorgeous stage by the sea. Finishes in Caminha at the mouth of the Minho River.
Cross the Minho River by boat to A Guarda. Short stage, ideal for resting or exploring the Santa Trega Celtic hill fort.
Spectacular stretch right next to the sea. You pass the Monastery of Santa María de Oia, literally facing the ocean.
Follow the coast with continuous views of the Atlantic. Arrival in lively, historic Baiona.
Varied stage featuring coast, woodland trails, and urban sections. Arrival in Vigo.
Ups and downs with views of the estuary. In Redondela you join the inland Portuguese Way.
Forests, ancient stone paths, and a great pilgrim atmosphere. Arrival in Pontevedra.
Comfortable and green stage. End in Caldas de Reis, famous for its thermal waters.
Relaxed stretch through villages and woods. Arrival in Padrón.
Final stage to Santiago de Compostela, culminating at the Cathedral.

nombre: Coastal Portuguese Way from A Guarda
dificultadDesc: Easy. Predominantly coastal and flat profile with gentle slopes as it turns inland towards the ría.
descripcion: The Galician stretch of the Coastal Way starting in A Guarda, opposite the Minho estuary. Cliffs, seaside monasteries, the Vigo estuary, and historic towns all the way to Santiago.
descripcionLarga: The Coastal Portuguese Way from A Guarda allows pilgrims to travel along the entire southwestern coastline of Galicia while taking in breathtaking views over the Atlantic Ocean.
Starting from the picturesque fishing village of A Guarda and the iconic Monastery of Santa María de Oia, the route continues past historic Baiona, the city of Vigo, and the Redondela inlet.

From Redondela it joins the traditional Portuguese Way, passing monumental Pontevedra, the thermal spa town of Caldas de Reis, and the Jacobean cradle of Padrón to complete the distance required for the Compostela certificate.
epoca: All year (ideal in spring and summer)
puntosDestacados: Castro de Santa Trega and the fishing harbour of A Guarda
Monastery of Santa María de Oia facing ocean breakers
Monterreal Fortress and Baiona marina
Panoramic views of the Cíes Islands and Vigo estuary
Old quarter and Basilica of Santa María in Pontevedra
Thermal mineral springs in Caldas de Reis
Plaza del Obradoiro and Cathedral of Santiago

etapas.desc: Spectacular stretch right next to the sea. You pass the Monastery of Santa María de Oia, literally facing the ocean.
Follow the coast with continuous views of the Atlantic. Arrival in lively, historic Baiona.
Varied stage featuring coast, woodland trails, and urban sections. Arrival in Vigo.
Ups and downs with views of the estuary. In Redondela you join the inland Portuguese Way.
Forests, ancient stone paths, and a great pilgrim atmosphere. Arrival in Pontevedra.
Comfortable and green stage. End in Caldas de Reis, famous for its thermal waters.
Relaxed stretch through villages and woods. Arrival in Padrón.
Final stage to Santiago de Compostela, culminating at the Cathedral.

dificultadDesc: Moderate. Combines flat sections along the estuaries with inland stages featuring hills and remote rural areas.
descripcion: The historical route taken by northern European pilgrims arriving by sea in Galicia. Maritime estuaries, lush forests, and medieval towns such as Pontedeume and Betanzos.
descripcionLarga: The English Way was the maritime route used in the Middle Ages by pilgrims arriving from Great Britain, Ireland, and Scandinavia at the northern ports of Ferrol and A Coruña.
Starting at the historic port of Ferrol, the route winds along spectacular coastal rías before venturing into the dense green forests and tranquil farmland of the Galician interior.
Covering over 100 km, it allows walkers to earn the Compostela in under a week, visiting medieval jewels like Pontedeume and Betanzos, and experiencing the untamed solitude of Hospital de Bruma.
puntosDestacados: Departure from Curuxeiras port in Ferrol and coastal promenade
Medieval town of Pontedeume and historic stone bridge across the Eume river
Well-preserved medieval center and famous gastronomy in Betanzos
Passing through legendary Hospital de Bruma in serene nature
Lush native oak and chestnut forests
Exciting arrival at the Plaza del Obradoiro

etapas.desc: You start in Ferrol, departing from the port and following the estuary. A gentle stage, initially urban, gradually becoming rural. Perfect for getting into rhythm effortlessly.
Pleasant walk between small hamlets and green fields, keeping the estuary in sight for part of the way. Arrival in picturesque medieval Pontedeume.
First demanding stage. Right after departure there is a steep climb setting the tone for the day. Alternates woodland and country lanes. Finish in beautiful Betanzos.
The toughest stage of the route. Long, with elevation gain and secluded stretches. Very rural with few services, but intensely authentic. Requires good stamina.
More manageable stage following the previous day's effort. Forest paths, tranquility, and comfortable terrain. Arrival in Sigüeiro.
Straightforward final stretch, gradually becoming more urban as you approach. Excitement builds toward arrival at Plaza del Obradoiro in Santiago.

dificultadDesc: Moderate. Rural stages with deep tranquility, isolation, and some long distance days.
descripcion: The final section of the oldest pilgrimage trail in the world, starting from the bimillenary city of Lugo. Untamed nature, complete peace, and joining the French Way in Melide.
descripcionLarga: The Primitive Way is the original Jacobean route, first walked by King Alfonso II the Chaste in the 9th century. Its section from Lugo spans the required 100+ km to receive the Compostela.
The pilgrimage begins passing through the UNESCO World Heritage Roman Wall of Lugo, continuing along quiet country trails, authentic hamlets, and ancient forests.
In Melide, the Primitive Way joins the bustling French Way, offering vibrant pilgrim culture and great regional food before reaching the Cathedral in Santiago de Compostela.
puntosDestacados: Walking atop the Roman Wall of Lugo (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
Traditional hamlets and rustic paths of San Román da Retorta
Merging with the French Way in Melide and tasting traditional Galician octopus
Shady eucalyptus and oak forests around Arzúa and O Pedrouzo
First glimpse of the Cathedral towers from Monte do Gozo
Unforgettable finish in Plaza del Obradoiro in Santiago de Compostela

etapas.desc: Departure from the Roman wall of Lugo. Peaceful stage featuring rural tracks, woods, and tiny hamlets. Perfect to begin without excessive strain.
Long and somewhat demanding stage. Deep rural environment and a feeling of solitude. Arrival in Melide where the Primitive merges with the French Way.
Short and comfortable stage, ideal for recovery. Plenty of forest, solid terrain, and more pilgrims upon joining the French Way. Finishes in Arzúa.
Pleasant path through eucalyptus groves and well-kept trails. Gentle uphills. Arrival in O Pedrouzo, classic stop before the final day.
Final stage with a mix of woodlands and urban approaches. Memorable arrival in Santiago de Compostela.
